message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s how you can quickly find the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow (US EPA)** | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), forecast | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. |
| **AQICN (World Air Quality Index)** | Global AQI, historical data, maps | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. |
| **Local news outlets** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries | Check their weather or environment sections. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., Plume Labs, AirVisual) | Push notifications, health recommendations | Download from your app store and set your location. |

### Quick Tips for Checking Air Quality

1. **Open a browser** and go to one of the sites above.  
2. **Enter “Los Angeles”** or your specific ZIP code.  
3. **Look for the AQI value** (0–500).  
   - 0–50: Good  
   - 51–100: Moderate  
   - 101–150: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
   - 151–200: Unhealthy  
   - 201–300: Very Unhealthy  
   - 301–500: Hazardous  
4. **Check the pollutant breakdown** if you’re concerned about specific allergens or irritants.

If you’re planning outdoor activities, you can also set up alerts on your phone so you’ll be notified when the AQI rises above a threshold you’re comfortable with.
